results.what_changed: Wrapped the lookup value in TRIM(CLEAN(...)) and forced it to text with &"" so text/number mismatches and hidden spaces no longer break the match; XLOOKUP is used as a fallback (Excel 365/2021+).

results.whats_broken: The last argument TRUE makes VLOOKUP do an approximate match, which returns the wrong client's price and gives #N/A when the name sorts before the first entry.
results.why: VLOOKUP's fourth setting tells Excel whether you want an exact match or a rough one. TRUE means 'rough' - Excel stops at the closest name that is alphabetically before yours, so you often get a neighbour's price, and if your name comes before the very first name in the list you get #N/A. For looking up a client by surname you almost always want an exact match, which is FALSE.
results.what_changed: Changed the last argument from TRUE to FALSE so VLOOKUP only returns a price when the surname matches exactly.

results.whats_broken: MATCH can't find today's date in the header row, even though it looks like it's there.
results.why: The most common reason is that the dates in B1:AF1 are not real dates but text that looks like dates (for example, typed with a leading apostrophe or imported as text). MATCH compares values strictly, so a text 'date' will never equal the real date returned by TODAY(). Another possibility is that the header contains a full date with a time part (e.g. 05.02.2026 00:00) while TODAY() has no time, so they don't match exactly.
results.what_changed: Wraps the header range in DATEVALUE so text dates are converted to real dates before matching. If your Excel version doesn't support array DATEVALUE, use =MATCH(TODAY(),INDEX(--$B$1:$AF$1,0),0) or convert the header cells to real dates (select them, Data > Text to Columns > Finish).

results.whats_broken: Some cells in columns B and C contain text instead of real times, so the subtraction fails with #VALUE!.
results.why: Excel can only subtract numbers or genuine time values. If someone typed something like '9-30' or '9.30' or added extra spaces, Excel treats that cell as text, and (C2-B2) returns #VALUE!. The rows that show a negative number are probably cases where the end time was entered earlier than the start time (for example a night shift crossing midnight), which is a separate issue.
results.what_changed: Wrapped the calculation in MOD(...,1) so shifts crossing midnight give a positive duration, and added a text check so bad entries are flagged instead of showing #VALUE!.
results.if_ok_suggestion: Better long-term fix: force proper time entry with Data > Data Validation (Time), and format B and C as Time so nobody can type free text.
